title: Tiny API
subtitle: A first simulation
summary: The smallest complete simulation: servers and a database, one traffic spike, one mission. Copy it as a starting point.

knobs.label: API servers
knobs.help: Each server handles 2 requests at a time.

hint.nudge: The servers reached {peak.api}% busy while the database was at {peak.db}%.
hint.idea: A server is busy for the whole request, including the time it waits for the database.
hint.lever: Work out how many requests per second the servers can take, then how many you need for the peak.
hint.step: One request keeps a server for about {= round(hold.api)} ms, so one server takes about {= round(2000 / hold.api)} requests per second; the peak is {peakRps}. Try {to} servers.

knobs.label: Database connections
knobs.help: Queries run in parallel up to this number.

hint.nudge: The database was at {peak.db}% busy at the peak. What is every request waiting for?
hint.idea: When all connections are busy, queries wait in line and the servers wait with them.
hint.lever: Compare the queries per second at the peak with how many one connection can run.
hint.step: One query takes about 20 ms, so one connection runs 50 per second; the peak sends {peakRps}. Try {to} connections.

lesson.intro: A small service answers requests. When traffic jumps, something runs out. Find what, and fix it without overspending.

missions.title: Survive the spike
missions.brief: The service runs on one server and two database connections. Traffic is about to triple. Keep it quick and keep failures rare, inside the budget.
missions.lesson: Every request holds a server while it waits for the database, so both have to be sized for the peak, and neither alone is enough.
